utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I said in French "concision is an art that one day or the other --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... On the suggested scheduling order.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, with regard to the agenda, the schedule, we are totally in agreement. But as the Prosecution intends to have more time, to write more pages, we clearly said that for us it's no. We will stick to the 200 pages. We won't have the time to read 400 pages, and we don't have the desire or the time to listen to the Prosecution for two days. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That means that the -- may I ask you --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll accept your decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If the Prosecution would be granted more time or more pages, would the Defence would like to have more pages and more time as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To my right I heard "naravno" which means "of course."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Because you said that a good listener would need only a few words.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We then will decide in due course on the request by the Prosecution to have more time and more pages available for their closing argument and the final brief. Then there's one remaining issue the Chamber asks the parties to pay specific attention to in their final briefs: The parties agree, as far as we can read it, on the applicability of the relevant provisions of Protocol I to the Geneva Conventions. The Prosecution has dealt with the matter in more detail; whereas, the Defence was rather general in this respect. The Chamber would very much like the parties to specifically address the issue why the parties consider Additional Protocol I applicable. Is it on the basis of customary law? Is it on the basis of the protocol itself binding as treaty law the parties, or is it on the basis of any special agreement or agreements whereby either Protocol I or parts of Protocol I were agreed to be binding upon the parties? If I am saying "the parties," the Chamber would very much like the parties in the trial to be very clear when they refer to "parties" which they are referring to parties to the conflict or to state parties, to agreements. And if the parties would rely on special agreements, the Chamber would like to have as precise as possible detailed information such as to -- between whom these special agreement or special agreements were concluded and when they were concluded, when these agreements entered into force. So full details on the applicability of Additional Protocol I. Is there anything else the parties would like to raise at this moment? Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Just to clarify things. I think you are referring here particularly to the agreement - I won't say between the parties - but the agreement reached around the 22nd May. I think that's what you're referring to. So that we make sure we're talking about the same thing. Or you are referring to something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is an agreement that has been specifically mentioned by the Prosecution. But whatever other special agreement or agreements you'd like to refer to, it's up to the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the Chamber would like detailed information in respect of the position taken by the parties in respect of the applicability of Additional Protocol I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then last Friday we discussed the submissions still to be expected by the parties on, if I might say, the list of exhibits. First Prosecution, whatever has been added to the memo that is already on our desk, and then to be filed so that it's part of the proceedings. Then we expect from the Defence a response not later than the end of this week so that we can give a decision on the admission of those documents. And it also pertains to the report of Professor Radinovic. Yes. Is there any other issue to be discussed at this very moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. But since we are probably not going to have any more opportunity to meet in the courtroom in the following hours, the Defence wishes to say very clearly in principle what they think about the witness, the expert witness Radinovic, very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could do that very briefly. Because I expect that part of the submission that we expect from the Prosecution deals with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But please take a couple of minutes to deal with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Simply, the most important thing in our view is that we believe that the request of the Prosecution to exclude a certain number of evidence concerning the expert report is not actually fair. Why? You know how long this list is. Six pages, very detailed, every point is mentioned. Of course -- [In English] 16 pages.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 16 pages. Apologies of the English booth.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 16 pages, very long, very detailed. A lot of time was needed for this. And, Your Honour, this was communicated to us after the testimony of Witness Radinovic. What the Prosecution was supposed to do in accordance with Rule 90(H) was the following: If they wanted to exclude these elements, they should have asked the witness why this was not included, what this document was about, et cetera. They didn't do so because they wanted to save on their time. They could have proceeded different. However, we were limited in our time in the same way and we, as you could see, were unable to present all of our documents as we wished to because simply speaking, Mr. President - and I insist on this - you certainly had your own reasons indicated to the Defence that if you presented all your documents as you wished to, we wouldn't have enough time with this witness. So we decided on a certain policy in accordance with your decision not to present all of these elements. The Prosecution wishes to take advantage of this because they were able to proceed in a different way. This is not logical. The expert report is a whole. This whole has to be accepted as such. And the expert witness repeated under oath that he has reviewed a very important volume of documents and that the BH army documents were appropriate, that they conform, and he was able to compare them with the SRK documents. They were comparable and they could function together. And as a conclusion, Mr. President - very briefly - this request is actually not acceptable in our view and it is not loyal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any need to respond, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just some short points. The Prosecution made abundantly clear before Mr. Radinovic entered the witness box what its concerns were. There was much correspondence and oral submissions on the point. It was for the Defence to address those identified issues. The witness, further, in cross-examination made clear that he had no recollection or no notes in relation to many of the matters which appeared in his expert report. That's all I wish to say on that, Mr. President. And one remaining matter is the filing. Perhaps we might refer to it as the amicus filing. I'd be grateful for some indication as to what you wish, if anything, from the Prosecution by way of a response to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The amicus filing of ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: There was a filing approximately two or three weeks ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But has there not yet been a decision taken on that where the parties were in a position to submit whatever they intended to submit and does not this decision say that the Chamber has not received any submissions from the parties in respect of this amicus curiae?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I remember that you said that if we wanted to we could, and everybody is free to make their own decisions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ierace, I think there is a written decision on that in which I think both for substantive reasons but also for formal reasons the application is rejected.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any other issue at this very moment? Then may I ask the Defence whether they have oriented themselves on the availability of Dr. Dunjic in case the Chamber would allow Dr. Dunjic to testify, the availability early next week?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tuesday and Wednesday are still the days that the Chamber has in mind?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's what we indicated as the days we had in mind. Not both of them, of course. It should be only a limited -- it should take only a limited time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will give you our response, Your Honour, as soon as possible, within a few hours, I think, through Madam Registrar, whom we thank for her help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it, Mr. Ierace, is the availability of Mr. Tait-Harris any problem, well, let's say, during the next ten days if he would be recalled?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't know. I'll check and inform Madam Registrar if that's convenient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since there seems to be nothing else on the agenda for this moment -- Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. You never disappoint me. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Until the very last day, regrettably, Mr. President. But my only question is: Could we get a response from the Prosecution about the communication of these photographs, because I don't know whether it's technically possible. I know that the assistant of the Prosecution didn't know for sure whether she was allowed to talk to the witness about it. That's how I understood her. So technically speaking, is it possible to send these photographs electronically?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any problem in that respect, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. I've spoken to my assistant, and she will make available to the Defence reasonably quickly, perhaps in the next hour or so, a CD or some floppy disks with the photographs in electronic form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And do we get written -- do we get coloured paper copies as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The latest on that, Mr. President, is that we expect we will have those available by 5.30. They have to be actually sent out of the OTP to be done, so we're expecting them back by 5.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was my following question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we will adjourn. And it is uncertain to exactly when, because it depends on the decisions of the Chamber, whether a recall of Mr. Tait-Harris and evidence in rejoinder by Dr. Dunjic will be permitted. If we would hear new evidence, if we would hear -- if Mr. Tait-Harris would be re-examined and if we would accept evidence in rejoinder to be presented, we would start on April the 1st in the afternoon, quarter past 2.00, unless we receive from the parties a message that Dr. Dunjic would not be available. Then the parties will be informed about the exact time when the expert witness will be examined.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one request, Mr. President, because for reasons related solely to my family, I will not be here on the 1st of April. I know that it might be embarrassing to even ask for it now, but is it possible to change the schedule at this point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since the Chamber expects the evidence, if the Defence will be allowed to present it, will not -- certainly not take much time. And the Chamber has no objection to scheduled for Wednesday. But before giving a decision, Mr. Ierace, you have an opportunity to express yourself on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Wednesday is fine, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If, however, you would not be available on Wednesday either, then lead counsel, of course, has to -- has to fulfil the duties of the Defence. So we'll presumably adjourn until the 2nd of April, 2.15 in the afternoon in this same courtroom, unless the parties will be informed otherwise through the registry. We'll adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
